headings.title: Department duties to serve children and families as a unit
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department of social services to address needs of homeless, dependent, and neglected children in the least restrictive setting.

headings.title: Authorized regional child assessment centers eligible for state funds
headings.reviewNote: Lists the sixteen approved regional child assessment centers eligible to receive state departmental funding.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 210.001 requiring social services to serve homeless and neglected children in the least restrictive setting and listing state-funded regional child assessment centers.

headings.title: Mandatory immunization for child care facility enrollment
headings.reviewNote: Bars enrollment in day care centers or preschools caring for ten or more children without proof of adequate ACIP immunizations.

headings.title: Exceptions for ongoing immunization process or exemptions
headings.reviewNote: Permits enrollment if immunizations are in progress, if a physician certifies a medical exemption or a parent files a written objection, or for 30 days if the child is homeless or in children's division custody.

headings.title: Outbreak control measures under health regulations
headings.reviewNote: Requires facility administrators during an outbreak or suspected outbreak of a vaccine-preventable disease to follow control measures instituted under Rule 19 CSR 20-20.040.

headings.title: Immunization recordkeeping and January 15 annual summary
headings.reviewNote: Requires facility administrators to maintain immunization records for every child, submit an annual summary report by January 15, and make records available to department personnel.

headings.title: Definition of satisfactory evidence of immunization
headings.reviewNote: Defines satisfactory evidence of immunization as a statement, certificate, or record from a physician or recognized health facility verifying vaccine type and administration date.

headings.title: Political subdivision authority for stricter preschool rules
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that this section does not preclude any political subdivision from adopting more stringent immunization rules for preschool children.

headings.title: Parental notice of right to inquire about exemptions
headings.reviewNote: Requires day care centers, preschools, and nursery schools to notify parents at enrollment (and beginning December 1, 2015, for current enrollees) that they may request notice of whether any enrolled children have immunization exemptions on file, and to provide such notice upon request.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 7 subsections for 210.003 requiring child care immunizations, conditional enrollment and exemption exceptions, outbreak control measures, administrator recordkeeping and annual reporting, satisfactory evidence definition, local authority, and parental exemption-inquiry notices.

headings.title: Prenatal and birth blood testing and newborn treatment
headings.reviewNote: Requires obstetric providers, if the woman consents, to take venous blood samples at first prenatal exam (or within 20 days), at 28 weeks, and immediately after birth for syphilis, hepatitis B, hepatitis C, HIV, and prescribed disorders, and mandates maternal treatment and newborn hepatitis B vaccine/HBIG.

headings.title: Department rules for FDA-approved tests and no fee bar
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department of health and senior services to make rules for FDA-approved or accepted tests and prohibits denying department testing based on inability to pay.

headings.title: Compliance with section 431.061 consent provisions
headings.reviewNote: Requires all persons providing care under this section to do so pursuant to section 431.061.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 210.030 governing consented prenatal and birth blood testing for syphilis, hepatitis B, hepatitis C, and HIV, department testing rules with no inability-to-pay denial, and compliance with section 431.061.

headings.title: Mandatory prophylactic eye drops for newborn infants
headings.reviewNote: Requires an attending physician, midwife, or nurse to drop a state-approved prophylactic medication into the eyes of a newborn infant.

headings.title: Parental or legal guardian objection exception
headings.reviewNote: Exempts eye-drop administration if a parent or legal guardian objects on religious belief grounds (source note flags religious-belief clause does not appear in original rolls of S.B. 951, 2018).

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 210.070 mandating prophylactic eye drops at birth to prevent ophthalmia neonatorum and establishing parental objection procedures.

headings.title: Department compilation and distribution of unsafe product list
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department of elementary and secondary education quarterly to provide all licensed child-care facilities a comprehensive list of children's products identified by the CPSC as unsafe.

headings.title: Child-care facility duty to inspect and dispose of unsafe products
headings.reviewNote: Requires child-care facilities to review recall lists, inspect premises, and immediately remove or dispose of unsafe children's items.

headings.title: Department facility inspections for recalled and unsafe products
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to inspect child-care facilities for unsafe children's products during regular licensing inspections.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority for unsafe children's product enforcement
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to promulgate rules to administer and enforce unsafe children's product standards.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 210.1007 requiring distribution of unsafe children's product lists, facility disposal duties, department inspections, and administrative rulemaking.

headings.title: Establishment of statewide Amber Alert system
headings.reviewNote: Creates the statewide Amber Alert System to aid in identifying and locating an abducted child or abducted or missing African American youth.

headings.title: Definition of abducted child or missing African American youth
headings.reviewNote: Defines abducted child or abducted or missing African American youth through four criteria covering kidnapping, child kidnapping, ages 14 to under 18, and trafficking offenses.

headings.title: Department of public safety regional alert coordination
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department of public safety to develop alert regions, coordinate local law enforcement and broadcasters, and notify regional media if a local agency opts out.

headings.title: Participating state agencies and voluntary private entities
headings.reviewNote: Requires the system to include capable state agencies (at minimum DPS, highway patrol, MoDOT, DHSS, and Missouri lottery) along with voluntary broadcasters and private entities.

headings.title: Public safety authority to notify additional alert regions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department of public safety to notify other regions upon verifying that oversight committee activation criteria have been met.

headings.title: Optional participation by local police and broadcasters
headings.reviewNote: Provides that participation in an Amber alert system is entirely optional for local law enforcement agencies and federally licensed radio and television broadcasters.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor penalty for knowingly false alert report
headings.reviewNote: Makes knowingly making a false report that triggers an Amber alert a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Nondiscrimination requirement in system coordination
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits the department of public safety from discriminating based on race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, sex, disability, or familial status when coordinating the system.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 8 subsections for 210.1012 creating the Amber Alert System, defining covered abducted or missing youth, regional coordination, participating state agencies, interregional notice, optional local participation, class A misdemeanor false-report penalty, and nondiscrimination.

headings.title: Creation of Amber Alert System Oversight Committee
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Amber Alert System Oversight Committee within the department of public safety to monitor alert effectiveness.

headings.title: Composition and appointment of oversight committee members
headings.reviewNote: Specifies appointment of committee members including law enforcement officials, broadcasters, highway patrol, and agency heads.

headings.title: Four-year terms and initial staggered terms of members
headings.reviewNote: Establishes four-year terms for oversight committee members with staggered initial two-, three-, and four-year terms.

headings.title: Uncompensated service and actual expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Provides that oversight committee members serve without compensation but shall be reimbursed for actual and necessary expenses.

headings.title: Committee rulemaking authority and chapter 536 clause
headings.reviewNote: Requires the Amber alert system oversight committee to promulgate implementing rules subject to chapter 536 compliance and nonseverability after August 28, 2003.

headings.title: Permissive embedded URL in issued Amber alerts
headings.reviewNote: Permits Amber alerts issued in Missouri to include an embedded Uniform Resource Locator (URL) referencing additional online information or technological capabilities.

headings.title: HAILEY'S Law short title and MULES and REJIS integration
headings.reviewNote: Cites subsection 7 as HAILEY'S Law and mandates integrating the Amber alert system into MULES and REJIS to expedite child abduction reporting.

headings.title: Annual report to general assembly on alert system operations
headings.reviewNote: Requires the oversight committee to submit an annual report to the general assembly on or before January 1, 2020, and annually thereafter covering six specified items.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 8 subsections for 210.1014 creating the Amber Alert System Oversight Committee, 10-member composition, four-year terms, expense reimbursement, committee rulemaking, embedded alert URLs, HAILEY'S Law MULES/REJIS integration, and annual legislative reporting.

headings.title: Creation and mission of Trauma-Informed Care Task Force
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Trauma-Informed Care for Children and Families Task Force to promote trauma-informed support systems and interagency cooperation.

headings.title: Membership of trauma-informed care task force
headings.reviewNote: Specifies membership including six department directors, the child advocate director, six private-sector trauma-informed care appointees, six legislators, and the Missouri Juvenile Justice Association executive director.

headings.title: Incorporation of trauma-informed best practices framework
headings.reviewNote: Directs incorporating evidence-based and evidence-informed best practices including the Missouri Model for early trauma identification, expeditious referral, and trauma-informed environments.

headings.title: Department of social services staff and technical support
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department of social services to provide research, clerical, technical, and other services required by the task force.

headings.title: Expense reimbursement for task force members and staff
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the task force, its members, and assigned staff shall receive reimbursement for actual and necessary meeting expenses.

headings.title: Initial meeting deadline within two months of enactment
headings.reviewNote: Requires the task force to meet within two months of August 28, 2018.

headings.title: Report deadline to general assembly and joint committee
headings.reviewNote: Requires reporting a summary of activities and legislative recommendations to the general assembly and the section 21.771 joint committee by January 1, 2019.

headings.title: Termination of task force on January 1, 2019
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the Trauma-Informed Care for Children and Families Task Force terminates on January 1, 2019.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 8 subsections for 210.1030 creating the Trauma-Informed Care for Children and Families Task Force, membership, Missouri Model best practices, social services support, expense reimbursement, initial meeting deadline, January 1, 2019 report, and January 1, 2019 termination.

headings.title: Statutory definition of full school day
headings.reviewNote: Defines full school day as six hours under the guidance and direction of teachers for pupils in foster care or children placed for treatment in licensed residential care facilities by social services.

headings.title: Mandatory entitlement of foster children to full educational days
headings.reviewNote: Entitles each pupil in foster care or child placed in a licensed residential care facility by social services to a full school day unless the school district determines fewer hours are warranted.

headings.title: Commissioner of education as educational ombudsman for foster youth
headings.reviewNote: Designates the commissioner of education or designee as ombudsman for residential treatment children with final authority over school-day length discrepancies, requiring a full day pending decision.

headings.title: Preservation of federal IDEA rights and free public education
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that this section does not infringe on federal IDEA rights or due process (which control school-day decisions) or deny any Missouri-domiciled child free public education.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 210.1050 defining a six-hour full school day, entitling foster and residential-treatment children to a full day, designating the commissioner of education as ombudsman, and preserving federal IDEA rights.

headings.title: Definitions for child care criminal background checks
headings.reviewNote: Defines child care provider, child care staff member, criminal background check (FBI, NCIC NSOR, and 5-year state criminal/sex offender/abuse registries), department (DESE), and qualifying result.

headings.title: Pre-employment check requests and supervised provisional work
headings.reviewNote: Requires providers to request background checks prior to staff employment or presence, allows supervised provisional work after qualifying FBI or Missouri fingerprint results, and exempts non-oversight providers without independent access when accompanied.

headings.title: Staff responsibility for fees and actual-cost cap
headings.reviewNote: Makes criminal background check costs the staff member's responsibility (reimbursable at the provider's discretion) and caps fees at actual processing and administration costs.

headings.title: Mandatory disqualifying criminal offenses for child care employment
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates disqualifying criminal offenses including murder, felony child abuse, sex crimes, kidnapping, and violent felonies.

headings.title: Ineligibility of adult or adult-certified household members
headings.reviewNote: Renders household members 18 or older (or under 18 certified as an adult) ineligible to be present at a child care home during child care hours if any subsection 4 disqualification applies.

headings.title: Disqualification from funds for prior licensure sanctions
headings.reviewNote: Permits disqualifying a provider from state or federal child care funds if the provider or an adult household member (excluding in-child's-home care) had licensure refused, suspended, or revoked under section 210.221 or 210.496.

headings.title: Portability exemption for recent qualifying Missouri checks
headings.reviewNote: Exempts providers from requesting a new check if the staff member received a qualifying check from DESE, DHSS, or DSS within five years for another Missouri provider and was separated no more than 180 consecutive days.

headings.title: Notice of background check results and ineligibility findings
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to notify the facility of eligibility without criminal details, while providing full details to the applicant.

headings.title: Administrative appeal process for ineligibility determinations
headings.reviewNote: Establishes written appeal rights to challenge check accuracy or present mitigating evidence within ten days of notice.

headings.title: Frequent checks of family care and central child abuse registries
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to perform more frequent checks against the family care safety and child abuse registries.

headings.title: Emergency rulemaking authority and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes emergency administrative rulemaking subject to chapter 536 procedures and specifies nonseverability clause.

headings.title: Exemption for religious child care facilities without federal funding
headings.reviewNote: Exempts child care facilities under exclusive control of a religious organization (section 210.211(1)(18), as renumbered per source note) unless receiving federal child care funds other than CACFP (42 U.S.C. section 1766).

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 12 subsections for 210.1080 defining child care background check terms, requiring pre-employment requests and provisional supervision, capping fees, listing disqualifying offenses, barring disqualified household members, allowing fund disqualification and check portability, setting 45-day notices and appeals, permitting registry checks, authorizing emergency rules, and exempting non-federally-funded religious facilities.

headings.title: Establishment of statewide child protection system
headings.reviewNote: Directs the children's division to establish a comprehensive child protection system for the entire state.

headings.title: System principles of child safety and family preservation
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that the system shall promote child safety, family integrity, and risk reduction through assessments and services.

headings.title: Division duties, central registry, hotline, and community contracting
headings.reviewNote: Details division duties including central registry maintenance, 24/7 hotline operations, mandatory reporter confidentiality, and provider contracts.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 210.109 establishing the statewide child protection system, family preservation principles, central registry maintenance, investigations, and community contracting.

headings.title: State policy and core principles for child welfare services
headings.reviewNote: Establishes state policy promoting safety, permanence, family preservation, and community-based service partnerships.

headings.title: Provider evaluation tool, monthly data, and quarterly reports
headings.reviewNote: Directs establishing a state/federal-compliant case-management evaluation tool, collecting monthly metrics, publishing quarterly county provider reports, and using metrics to evaluate competitive contract bids.

headings.title: Fourteen-member response and evaluation team and duties
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a 14-member response and evaluation team meeting before January 1, 2021, to semiannually review the evaluation tool, review anomalous cases and incentives, conduct periodic field file reviews, and provide technical assistance.

headings.title: Performance-based contracting with private child-placing agencies
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes contracts with accredited private agencies for foster care, family preservation, and adoption services.

headings.title: National accreditation as prima facie licensure evidence
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division to accept COA, JCAH, or CARF accreditation as prima facie evidence of completing licensure requirements under sections 210.481 to 210.511.

headings.title: Performance-based payment models and financial incentives
headings.reviewNote: Directs implementation of performance-based payment models tied to timely family reunification and permanency.

headings.title: Immediate corrective actions and contract termination
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division to consider immediate best-interest actions including corrective plans, halting new referrals, transferring cases, or terminating a provider's contract.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and chapter 536 compliance
headings.reviewNote: Requires the children's division by July 1, 2021, to promulgate implementing rules subject to chapter 536 compliance and nonseverability after August 28, 2004.

headings.title: Voiding of contract clauses indemnifying state negligence
headings.reviewNote: Declares void and unenforceable any service provider contract clause indemnifying, holding harmless, or insuring the state for damages or injuries caused in whole or in part by the state's negligence.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 9 subsections for 210.112 establishing child welfare system principles, provider evaluation tool and quarterly reports, response and evaluation team, competitive contracting, accreditation prima facie licensure, cost/incentive payments, corrective actions, rulemaking, and voiding clauses indemnifying state negligence.

headings.title: Qualified immunity for contracted private child-placing agencies
headings.reviewNote: Grants private contracted children's services providers qualified civil immunity when the child is not in the contractor's physical care to the same extent as the children's division, except as provided in section 207.085.

headings.title: Exception for knowing violation of policy, rule, or law
headings.reviewNote: Excludes immunity if a private contractor knowingly violates a stated or written division policy, division rule, state law directly related to child abuse and neglect or division activities, or local property safety ordinance.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 210.114 granting qualified civil immunity to private child welfare contractors when the child is not in their physical care and excluding knowing violations of division policy, rules, child-abuse laws, or local safety ordinances.

headings.title: Mandatory duty to report suspected child abuse or neglect
headings.reviewNote: Lists mandated reporters and requires immediate reporting to the division upon reasonable cause to suspect child abuse or neglect, barring prior internal investigations and covering abuse by any person.

headings.title: Designated single report for medical institution teams
headings.reviewNote: Permits a designated member of a medical institution team with joint knowledge to make a single report, requiring any other member to report immediately if the designee fails to do so.

headings.title: Prohibition on employer or supervisor interference with reports
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits supervisors, administrators, or employers from impeding, discouraging, or altering employee child abuse reports.

headings.title: Religious medical-treatment exception and state authority
headings.reviewNote: Provides that withholding specified medical treatment based solely on legitimate parental religious beliefs does not alone justify an abuse/neglect finding or central registry entry, without limiting reports, investigations, or state authority to ensure needed medical care.

headings.title: Permissive reporting by any other person with suspicion
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes any person other than mandated reporters to report suspected child abuse or neglect in accordance with sections 210.109 to 210.183.

headings.title: Mandatory reporting of under-18 child deaths to coroner
headings.reviewNote: Requires mandated reporters with probable cause to suspect a child under 18 eligible for a live birth certificate has died to report to the medical examiner or coroner, who notifies the division and child fatality review panel.

headings.title: Permissive supplemental reporting to police or juvenile office
headings.reviewNote: Permits mandated reporters also to report suspected abuse or neglect to law enforcement or a juvenile office, without replacing reporting to the division.

headings.title: Reporting out-of-state victims or injuries to other state
headings.reviewNote: Permits mandated reporters to report suspected abuse or neglect of a nonresident child or out-of-state injury to the other state's child protection agency in lieu of Missouri's division if that agency accepts the report.

headings.title: Unaccompanied youth status alone not sufficient to report
headings.reviewNote: Provides that unaccompanied youth status under 42 U.S.C. section 11434a(6) is not alone sufficient basis for reporting unless the child is under 16 or incapacitated under section 475.010, without limiting abuse or neglect reporting.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 9 subsections for 210.115 enumerating mandated reporters and immediate reporting duties, medical team single reports, anti-interference and retaliation bars, religious medical-treatment exception, permissive reporting, under-18 death reporting to coroners, supplemental police reports, out-of-state reporting, and unaccompanied youth status limits.

headings.title: Prohibition on child placement in homes with registered sex offenders
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits reuniting or placing a child in a home where any resident has pled guilty to or been convicted of felony sex crimes.

headings.title: Division placement discretion for other chapter 566/568 crimes
headings.reviewNote: Grants the division discretion regarding placement when a parent or household resident was found guilty of other chapter 566 or 568 offenses not listed in subsection 1 or equivalent out-of-state child-victim offenses.

headings.title: One-thousand-foot residency bar for child who abused another
headings.reviewNote: Bars a child found by substantiated report to have abused another child from returning to or residing within 1,000 feet of the abused child's residence, child care facility, or school until a court finds no abuse occurred or the abused child turns 18 (excluding siblings or same-home children).

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 210.117 barring reunification or placement in homes with listed child-victim offenses, granting division discretion for other chapter 566/568 offenses, and imposing a 1,000-foot proximity bar for a child who abused another child.

headings.title: Listing in central registry upon judicial finding of child abuse
headings.reviewNote: Requires entering an individual onto the central child abuse registry upon a court finding of abuse by a preponderance of evidence.

headings.title: Mandatory registry listing upon criminal conviction or plea
headings.reviewNote: Requires courts to order central registry listing whenever a person pleads guilty to or is found guilty of listed chapter 565, 566, 567, 568, or 573 offenses (or attempts) involving children, with clerk transmission to the division (source note flags section 568.080/568.090 transfers).

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 210.118 requiring central registry listing upon preponderance-of-evidence abuse/neglect findings in chapter 210/211 actions and upon guilty pleas or convictions for listed criminal offenses against children.

headings.title: Program establishment and youth eligibility criteria
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department of social services to establish a comprehensive service, education, and residential care program for youth in division custody under age 21 whose needs cannot be met by existing state programs.

headings.title: Contracts with qualified Missouri-based service providers
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to contract for program operations with certified, licensed, or accredited Missouri-based qualified service providers or consortia with proven experience.

headings.title: Memoranda of understanding with state-owned facilities
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to enter into memoranda of understanding with appropriate state-owned facilities or campuses.

headings.title: Civil liability immunity for contracted clinical service providers
headings.reviewNote: Grants good-faith civil damages immunity absent gross negligence to contracted qualified service providers (excluding child abuse or neglect under section 210.110), void if the state creates a $1 million inflation-adjusted indemnification fund.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority for behavioral challenges program
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department of social services to adopt administrative rules to govern behavioral program standards.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsections for 210.119 establishing a severe behavioral challenges program and youth eligibility, authorizing contracts with Missouri providers and MOUs with state facilities, granting conditional civil immunity, and authorizing rulemaking.

headings.title: Short title of Erin's Law
headings.reviewNote: Designates sections 210.1200 and 210.1210 as Erin's Law.

headings.title: Creation and sixteen-member composition of task force
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Task Force on the Prevention of Sexual Abuse of Children and specifies all 16 state agency, law enforcement, school, court, and advocacy members.

headings.title: Member qualifications and statewide geographic diversity
headings.reviewNote: Requires task force members to be actively involved in child abuse prevention, treatment, and child welfare and reflect Missouri's geographic diversity.

headings.title: Election of presiding officer and calling of meetings
headings.reviewNote: Requires the task force to elect a presiding officer by majority vote and meet at the call of the presiding officer.

headings.title: Duties to gather information and make policy recommendations
headings.reviewNote: Directs the task force to recommend ways to reduce child sexual abuse and improve treatment by gathering statewide information, receiving reports and testimony, and creating state policy goals.

headings.title: Permissive statutory change and interagency proposals
headings.reviewNote: Permits recommendations to include specific statutory change proposals and methods to foster state agency and state-local cooperation.

headings.title: Mandatory consultation with state agencies and boards
headings.reviewNote: Requires the task force to consult with employees of social services, public safety, elementary and secondary education, and other state entities as necessary.

headings.title: Uncompensated service without expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Provides that task force members serve without compensation and shall not be reimbursed for their expenses.

headings.title: Annual progress reports to general assembly beginning 2019
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department of social services, collaborating with the task force beginning January 1, 2019, to submit yearly progress reports to the general assembly.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 9 subsections for 210.1200 enacting Erin's Law, creating the 16-member Task Force on the Prevention of Sexual Abuse of Children, qualifications, presiding officer, recommendation duties, statutory proposals, agency consultation, uncompensated service without reimbursement, and annual reports.

headings.title: Definitions for unaccompanied youth support services
headings.reviewNote: Defines service provider, shelter, supportive services (including 14 listed items), and unaccompanied youth under 42 U.S.C. section 11434a(6).

headings.title: Unaccompanied youth access to shelter and supportive services
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes verified unaccompanied youth to access emergency shelter and supportive services without parental consent.

headings.title: Acceptable documentation for verifying unaccompanied youth status
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates valid documentation including signed statements from social workers, homeless liaisons, or representing attorneys.

headings.title: Good-faith civil and criminal liability immunity for providers
headings.reviewNote: Immunizes persons relying in good faith on a subsection 3(1) verification statement without actual knowledge of fraud from civil or criminal liability for serving without parental consent, without relieving negligence or criminal liability.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 210.121 defining unaccompanied youth terms, service access, verification documentation, and service provider liability immunity.

headings.title: Task force policy recommendations to education officials
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes submitting recommendations to the education commissioner and state board regarding curricula, training, and parent notices.

headings.title: Curriculum topics, abuse warning signs, and counseling resources
headings.reviewNote: Details recommendation topics including student awareness, warning sign detection, intervention steps, and counseling resources.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 210.1210 authorizing sexual abuse task force policy recommendations to education officials and enumerating curriculum and counseling topics.

headings.title: Definition and scope of voluntary placement agreement
headings.reviewNote: Defines voluntary placement agreement allowing parent to retain legal custody while social services administers mental health care.

headings.title: Interagency agreement with department of mental health
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes social services to enter agreements with mental health to administer placement and defines mental health as a child-placing agency.

headings.title: Supervisory authority and compliance oversight of delegated care
headings.reviewNote: Requires social services to supervise delegated functions to ensure compliance with federal and state child welfare standards.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes administrative rulemaking subject to chapter 536 procedures and specifies nonseverability clause.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 210.122 defining voluntary placement agreements for children needing mental health care, interagency cooperation, supervision, and rulemaking nonseverability.

headings.title: Mandatory division physical custody upon discharge and reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Requires division to take physical custody of children discharged from hospital and pay inpatient daily rates upon failure to retrieve child.

headings.title: Authority to administer emergency psychiatric treatment
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes emergency rooms and receiving psychiatric facilities to administer emergency psychiatric treatment to children in division custody.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 210.1225 requiring division to take custody of hospitalized children upon discharge, hospital reimbursement, and emergency psychiatric treatment.

headings.title: Definitions of adult relative and temporary alternative placement
headings.reviewNote: Defines adult relative and temporary alternative placement agreement for voluntary out-of-home placement with relatives.

headings.title: Authority, purpose, and Missouri residency requirement
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes temporary alternative placement agreements to mitigate trauma and support short-term stability, requiring the child to reside in Missouri unless unavailable medical treatment requires another state.

headings.title: Home walk-through, background checks, and relative residency
headings.reviewNote: Requires a home walk-through and registry/court background checks (with discretionary fingerprinting) of the relative and adult household members, and requires the relative to reside in Missouri during the agreement.

headings.title: Six prerequisites, voluntariness, and five-day termination
headings.reviewNote: Sets six conditions for entering an agreement, states advising parents of potential legal action is not coercion, and requires at least five days' written notice to terminate.

headings.title: Relative decision-making authority and third-party immunity
headings.reviewNote: Grants the relative day-to-day, educational, and medical decision-making authority with parental/division consultation, requires a division notice form, and immunizes schools and providers relying on it (source note flags word 'letter' in H.B. 1414, 2020).

headings.title: Division monitoring, contacts, meetings, and juvenile report
headings.reviewNote: Requires close monitoring, at least twice-monthly personal child contacts, team decision-making meetings within 10 days and monthly, opening a family-centered services case within 10 days, and a written report to the juvenile office 10 days before termination.

headings.title: Referral to juvenile officer upon parental refusal
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division to refer the matter to the juvenile officer if the parent or guardian does not agree to the temporary alternative placement agreement.

headings.title: Diligent implementation and full cooperation duties
headings.reviewNote: Requires all parties to exercise diligent efforts to implement the agreement and requires the relative and parents or guardians to fully cooperate with the division.

headings.title: Referral to juvenile officer if goals are unmet
headings.reviewNote: Requires referring the case to the juvenile officer if agreement goals are not accomplished in time and child safety or well-being cannot be assured upon return home.

headings.title: Execution alongside juvenile informal adjustment process
headings.reviewNote: Permits executing a temporary alternative placement agreement in conjunction with the juvenile office informal adjustment process.

headings.title: Nonbinding effect on juvenile officer and required review
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the juvenile officer is not bound unless a signatory and retains legal discretion, but shall consider the agreement and its implementation.

headings.title: Mandatory regulations as condition of effective date
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division to promulgate implementing regulations and delays effectiveness of this section until regulations are promulgated.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 12 subsections for 210.123 governing temporary alternative placement agreements with adult relatives, Missouri residency, home walk-throughs and background checks, prerequisites and five-day termination, relative decision authority, division monitoring, juvenile officer referrals, cooperation, informal adjustment, nonbinding effect on juvenile officers, and mandatory regulations.

headings.title: Request to juvenile officer to take protective custody
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a police officer, law enforcement official, or physician with reasonable cause to suspect abuse or neglect to request that the juvenile officer take the child into protective custody under chapter 211.

headings.title: Temporary protective custody without parental consent
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a police officer, law enforcement official, or physician to take or retain temporary protective custody without parental consent upon reasonable cause of imminent serious physical harm or threat to life before court or juvenile officer action.

headings.title: Notifications, twelve-hour statement, and division bar
headings.reviewNote: Requires immediate notice to the juvenile officer and division, reasonable attempt to advise parents, a written statement within 12 hours, and juvenile officer action, while barring division employees from removing a child on their own.

headings.title: Twenty-four-hour limit absent juvenile court order
headings.reviewNote: Limits temporary protective custody under this section to 24 hours unless extended by an order of the juvenile court.

headings.title: Definition of temporary protective custody and detention bar
headings.reviewNote: Defines temporary protective custody as placement in a hospital, medical facility, emergency foster care, or court-directed placement, prohibiting secure detention of an abused or neglected child.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsections for 210.125 governing protective custody requests, emergency temporary custody without parental consent, immediate notices and 12-hour written statements with a division self-removal bar, 24-hour cap, and placement definition excluding secure detention.

headings.title: Designation of department as state notification agency
headings.reviewNote: Designates the department as the notification agency for all license-exempt residential care facilities under sections 210.1250 to 210.1286.

headings.title: Mandatory parental and legal guardian access to children
headings.reviewNote: Requires residential care facilities to allow parents or guardians unencumbered access to their children without requiring prior notification to the facility.

headings.title: Statutory duty of facilities to provide adequate care and nutrition
headings.reviewNote: Requires residential care facilities to provide adequate food, clothing, shelter, medical, and other care necessary for the child's physical and mental health.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 210.1256 designating social services as notification agency for residential facilities, guaranteeing parental access, and requiring adequate care.

headings.title: Mandatory written notice of operation by facility director
headings.reviewNote: Requires directors of residential facilities caring for children to submit written notice of operation to the department.

headings.title: Three-month registration deadline for existing facilities
headings.reviewNote: Requires all residential care facilities operating on July 14, 2021, to register within three months after July 14, 2021.

headings.title: Exemption for equivalently regulated licensed facilities
headings.reviewNote: Exempts already-licensed residential care facilities so long as their existing license, registration, or monitoring imposes all requirements of sections 210.1250 to 210.1286.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 210.1259 requiring pre-acceptance facility notification, a three-month registration deadline for facilities operating on July 14, 2021, and an exemption for equivalently regulated licensed facilities.

headings.title: Mandatory diligent search for biological parents upon state custody
headings.reviewNote: Requires the children's division to conduct a diligent search to identify and locate biological parents of children taken into custody.

headings.title: Definition of diligent search and court hearing reports
headings.reviewNote: Defines diligent search as an exhaustive effort initiated immediately to identify and locate an unknown biological parent, with search progress reported at each court hearing until located or excused by the court.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 210.127 requiring diligent search for biological parents upon protective custody and specifying search documentation in case records.

headings.title: Department petition for injunctive relief against noncompliant facilities
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to petition the circuit court for injunctive relief against facilities operating in violation of standards.

headings.title: Three-business-day hearing on ex parte cease-operation orders
headings.reviewNote: Requires a hearing within three business days of an ex parte cease-operation order under subsection 1, with attempted notice and due process, to decide if reasonable cause persists.

headings.title: Department notice to attorney general upon removal referral
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to notify the attorney general of any referral to a juvenile officer for child removal from a residential care facility, including subsection 1 violations.

headings.title: Five-day emergency temporary protective custody order
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the court upon juvenile officer referral, division placement certification, and three written findings to place a child in division emergency custody for up to five days before exclusive juvenile court jurisdiction attaches.

headings.title: UCCJEA procedures for out-of-state or foreign children
headings.reviewNote: Applies sections 452.700 to 452.930 and section 452.755 procedures for residential-facility children from another state or country or under another state's court jurisdiction.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsections for 210.1271 authorizing circuit court injunctive relief for four facility violations, three-business-day hearings on ex parte cease-operation orders, attorney general notifications, five-day emergency temporary custody orders, and UCCJEA procedures for out-of-state children.

headings.title: Immediate oral report to central telephone hotline
headings.reviewNote: Requires immediate oral reports of suspected child abuse or neglect to the central division hotline or local office.

headings.title: Required contents of child abuse and neglect reports
headings.reviewNote: Details required report information including child identities, addresses, nature of injuries, family composition, and reporter details.

headings.title: Mandatory twenty-four hour transmission of sexual abuse evidence
headings.reviewNote: Mandates turning over all evidence of sexual abuse of children under eighteen to the division within twenty-four hours.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 210.130 governing oral child abuse reports, required report contents, and mandatory twenty-four hour transmission of child sexual abuse evidence.

headings.title: Civil and criminal liability immunity for reporters and officials
headings.reviewNote: Grants broad civil and criminal immunity to persons making reports, taking photos, or retaining children in good faith.

headings.title: Civil liability immunity for child assessment center personnel
headings.reviewNote: Immunizes employees and contractors of state-funded child assessment centers from civil liability absent bad faith.

headings.title: Immunity for citizens reporting school employee child abuse
headings.reviewNote: Grants immunity to persons reporting school employee abuse to school officials, excluding knowingly false reports.

headings.title: Mandatory preliminary division evaluation upon child fatality
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division to conduct a three-day evaluation of hotline workers, case workers, and circuit managers following a child death.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 210.135 granting immunity from civil and criminal liability for reporting abuse, child assessment center employee immunity, school reporting immunity, and preliminary worker evaluations upon child fatalities.

headings.title: Confidentiality of minor child care identifying records
headings.reviewNote: Declares personally identifiable information of minors receiving child care confidential and protected from public disclosure.

headings.title: State agency disclosure exceptions for administration and law
headings.reviewNote: Permits disclosure between state agencies for administrative, statistical, or law enforcement investigative purposes.

headings.title: Parental and guardian access to child records
headings.reviewNote: Protects parents and legal guardians right to access child care records regarding their own minor child.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 210.1360 establishing confidentiality of personally identifiable information for minors receiving child care, state agency exceptions, and parental access.

headings.title: Petition for court order to produce child from facility
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes child protection or law enforcement to petition court to order an exempt facility to present a child for assessment.

headings.title: Judicial standard and grounds for entry of production order
headings.reviewNote: Directs court to issue production order upon finding reasonable cause that child safety or health is at risk.

headings.title: Assessment completion and return of child to facility
headings.reviewNote: Requires completing the assessment and returning the child unless protective custody or court detention is warranted.

headings.title: Judicial authority to expand order to all facility children
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes expanding the order to require production of other children residing at the facility when pervasive risks exist.

headings.title: Ex parte petition and order upon risk of child removal
headings.reviewNote: Allows ex parte orders if notice would trigger child concealment, flight, or immediate danger.

headings.title: Subpoena compliance and protective disclosures
headings.reviewNote: Governs service of subpoenas and petitions without requiring disclosure of confidential reporter identities.

headings.title: Jurisdiction and venue in juvenile or family court
headings.reviewNote: Places venue in the juvenile or family court of the county where the residential facility is located.

headings.title: Expedited judicial proceedings to protect child safety
headings.reviewNote: Mandates expedited court scheduling and priority handling of petitions to ensure child protection.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor penalty for knowing violation of order
headings.reviewNote: Classifies knowingly concealing a child or violating a judicial production order as a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Tolling of investigation timelines during subpoena petitions
headings.reviewNote: Tolls the children's division investigation and notification time frames under sections 210.145, 210.152, and 210.183 while a subpoena petition is pending until full production, withdrawal, or quashing.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 10 subsections for 210.143 authorizing court orders to present children from exempt residential facilities, judicial standards, 72-hour assessments, order expansion, ex parte orders, protective-order motions, venue, expedited proceedings, class A misdemeanor penalty, and subpoena timeline tolling.

headings.title: Establishment of child abuse hotline and priority protocols
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division to develop hotline protocols prioritizing child safety, speedy response, and family assessment.

headings.title: Structured decision-making and standard risk assessment tools
headings.reviewNote: Directs the division to use structured decision-making protocols and standardized risk assessments for reports.

headings.title: Hotline screening and investigation determination criteria
headings.reviewNote: Governs determining whether a report warrants formal child abuse investigation or family assessment.

headings.title: Jurisdiction based on child or perpetrator Missouri residency
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes accepting reports if either the subject child or alleged perpetrator resides in or is located in Missouri.

headings.title: Transmission of non-resident reports to out-of-state agencies
headings.reviewNote: Directs forwarding reports involving non-resident children and perpetrators to the appropriate out-of-state agency.

headings.title: Mandatory review upon three hotline calls within 72 hours
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division, upon three or more calls within 72 hours concerning the same child, to review whether the calls meet report criteria and contact callers to assess harassment.

headings.title: Immediate notification to law enforcement of criminal allegations
headings.reviewNote: Mandates immediate local office notification to law enforcement upon receiving reports alleging criminal child abuse.

headings.title: Investigation initiation timelines and in-person child contact
headings.reviewNote: Requires initiating investigations within twenty-four hours and conducting prompt in-person child interviews.

headings.title: Designation of chief investigator for each local office
headings.reviewNote: Directs the division director to appoint a chief investigator in each local office to oversee criminal investigations.

headings.title: Required scope and factual components of child investigations
headings.reviewNote: Details investigation scope including nature of injury, home conditions, risk factors, and perpetrator interview.

headings.title: Forty-eight-hour follow-up contact with mandated reporters
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division to contact any section 210.115 mandated reporter within 48 hours of receiving a report to ensure full information and obtain pertinent medical records.

headings.title: Investigation referral to prosecutor upon suspected malicious report
headings.reviewNote: Directs notifying law enforcement and prosecutors if an investigation reveals a knowingly false or malicious report.

headings.title: Use of multidisciplinary teams in child investigations
headings.reviewNote: Requires utilizing multidisciplinary teams for sexual abuse, severe physical injury, or child fatality reviews.

headings.title: Family support team meetings and permitted attendee rights
headings.reviewNote: Governs family support team meetings, permitting parents to bring advocates, attorneys, or supportive family members.

headings.title: Transition from investigation to family assessment approach
headings.reviewNote: Directs switching to a family assessment and services approach if completing an investigation is not appropriate, requiring prior written notice to local law enforcement with documented reasons.

headings.title: Voluntary family assessment and provision of supportive services
headings.reviewNote: Governs family assessments focusing on family strengths and voluntary supportive services without registry listing.

headings.title: Forty-five day investigation completion and status update
headings.reviewNote: Requires updating case records and providing status notifications within forty-five days of the initial report.

headings.title: Reporter right to receive investigation outcome information
headings.reviewNote: Entitles mandated reporters and reporting individuals to receive written notice of investigation findings and case status.

headings.title: Information on office of child advocate for dissatisfied persons
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division to provide any individual dissatisfied with investigation results information about the office of child advocate and its services under sections 37.700 to 37.730.

headings.title: Admissibility of child abuse reports in child custody proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Governs evidentiary admissibility and judicial consideration of hotline reports in family court custody cases.

headings.title: Coinvestigation and record sharing with other jurisdictions
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that this chapter does not prohibit coinvestigating or sharing records with child welfare, law enforcement, or judicial officers of another state, territory, or nation under section 210.150(4).

headings.title: No registry entry for section 211.031(1)(1)(d) jurisdiction
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits entering a child's parent, guardian, or custodian into the central registry when a court takes custody jurisdiction based on need of services under section 211.031(1)(1)(d).

headings.title: Division rulemaking authority for hotline and investigation procedures
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the division to promulgate administrative rules to implement hotline and investigative standards.

headings.title: Rulemaking compliance with chapter 536 and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Conditioned validity of rules on chapter 536 procedures and specifies nonseverability clause.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 24 subsections for 210.145 establishing hotline protocols, risk and joint safety assessments, investigation screening, jurisdiction, multi-call reviews, law enforcement notice, initiation timelines, chief investigators, mandated reporter follow-up, MDTs, family support team meetings, assessment transitions, 45/90/120-day timelines, reporter rights, child advocate info, custody admissibility, out-of-state coinvestigation, registry exclusion, and rulemaking.

headings.title: SAFE CARE provider evaluation for children three and under
headings.reviewNote: Requires any merited abuse or neglect investigation involving a child three years of age or younger to include an evaluation or case-file/photograph review by a section 334.950 SAFE CARE provider.

headings.title: Mandatory referral to juvenile officer upon SAFE CARE finding
headings.reviewNote: Mandates immediate division referral to the juvenile officer with care, safety, and placement recommendations when a SAFE CARE provider diagnoses physical abuse in a child three years of age or younger.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 210.146 requiring SAFE CARE provider medical evaluations for infant injuries and mandatory referral to juvenile officers.

headings.title: Confidentiality of family support team discussions and records
headings.reviewNote: Declares information and discussions at family support team meetings confidential, subject to protective disclosure rules.

headings.title: Signed form documenting core commitments and meeting agreements
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division to develop a written form signed at meeting conclusion documenting agreed core commitments and action plans.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 210.147 establishing confidentiality of family support team meetings and requiring signed core commitment forms.

headings.title: Assessment protocol for juveniles with problem sexual behavior
headings.reviewNote: Governs hotline reports involving youth displaying problem sexual behavior, directing assessment rather than registry listing.

headings.title: Preservation of local division formal investigation authority
headings.reviewNote: Preserves division authority to initiate formal investigations if safety risks or noncompliance emerge.

headings.title: Definition of juvenile with problem sexual behavior
headings.reviewNote: Defines juvenile with problem sexual behavior as any person under fourteen years of age who has allegedly committed sexual abuse against another child.

headings.title: Division rulemaking authority for problem sexual behavior protocols
headings.reviewNote: Directs the division to promulgate rules within 180 days to implement assessment and treatment protocols.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 210.148 establishing procedures for reports involving juveniles with problem sexual behavior, definitions, investigation authority, and rulemaking.

headings.title: Confidential status of child abuse and neglect reports and records
headings.reviewNote: Mandates strict confidentiality for all child protection records and hotline reports made under sections 210.110 to 210.165.

headings.title: Authorized persons permitted access to central registry records
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates specific entities permitted access to central registry records, including law enforcement, courts, and licensing agencies.

headings.title: Authorized access to unsubstantiated and assessment records
headings.reviewNote: Lists eight categories of persons permitted access to section 210.152 records determined to have insufficient evidence or handled through family assessment, including division staff, victims, alleged perpetrators, fatality panels, criminal justice, providers with consent, researchers, and DoD family advocacy staff.

headings.title: Criminal misdemeanor penalty for unauthorized record disclosure
headings.reviewNote: Classifies knowingly disclosing confidential child welfare records without authorization as a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Public disclosure of findings in child fatality and near-fatality cases
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes public release of investigative summaries and findings in cases resulting in child fatality or near-fatality.

headings.title: Mandatory reporting of findings to DoD family advocacy program
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division to report its findings to the relevant U.S. Department of Defense family advocacy program or authorized 10 U.S.C. section 1787 recipient when a suspected perpetrator or caretaker is a military or Armed Forces member.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsections for 210.150 establishing confidentiality of child abuse records, central registry access lists, unsubstantiated and family assessment record access, class A misdemeanor disclosure penalty, fatality/near-fatality discretionary release, and mandatory DoD family advocacy reporting.

headings.title: Law enforcement duties upon locating suspected sex trafficking victim
headings.reviewNote: Requires law enforcement locating a suspected child victim of sex trafficking or severe trafficking (22 U.S.C. section 7102) to report immediately under section 210.115 and ensure safety and coinvestigate with the division.

headings.title: Temporary protective custody without parental consent
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes law enforcement to take or retain temporary protective custody under section 210.125 without parental consent upon reasonable cause of imminent serious physical harm or threat to life from sex trafficking or sexual exploitation.

headings.title: Least restrictive safe placement for children in division custody
headings.reviewNote: Requires law enforcement and the children's division to secure placement in the least restrictive setting to protect from further trafficking any child already under section 211.031(1)(1)(a) jurisdiction and division custody.

headings.title: Child advocacy center referral, SAFE CARE, and screening
headings.reviewNote: Requires referral to a child advocacy center for a forensic interview, medical evaluation by a SAFE CARE provider as necessary, and assessment using a validated sex-trafficking screening tool.

headings.title: Mandatory use of multidisciplinary teams in trafficking cases
headings.reviewNote: Mandates using multidisciplinary teams including forensic interviewers and victim advocates in sex trafficking investigations.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsections for 210.1500 mandating immediate reporting and coinvestigation of suspected child sex trafficking, authorizing temporary protective custody, requiring least restrictive safe placement for children in custody, mandating CAC/SAFE CARE/screening referrals, and requiring multidisciplinary teams.

headings.title: Creation and purpose of statewide anti-trafficking council
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Statewide Council Against Adult Trafficking and the Commercial Sexual Exploitation of Children within the attorney general's office.

headings.title: Council quorum, creation timeline, and quarterly meetings
headings.reviewNote: Establishes majority quorum, requires creation within 30 days of August 28, 2026, first meeting within 30 days, at least quarterly meetings, and permits forming subgroups.

headings.title: Appointment and executive duties of council executive director
headings.reviewNote: Directs the attorney general to appoint an executive director to manage council operations and administer anti-trafficking programs.

headings.title: Commercial Sexual Exploitation of Children Fund creation and use
headings.reviewNote: Creates a dedicated state treasury fund to hold appropriations, federal grants, and donations for victim services.

headings.title: Establishment of Committee on Sex and Human Trafficking Training
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a specialized training committee within the council to evaluate and approve human trafficking curricula.

headings.title: Composition of sex and human trafficking training committee
headings.reviewNote: Specifies committee membership including representatives from law enforcement, health professions, education, and legal services.

headings.title: Attorney general representative as committee chairperson
headings.reviewNote: Directs the attorney general's representative to serve as chairperson of the training committee.

headings.title: Uncompensated service and travel expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Provides that committee members serve without compensation but may receive actual travel expense reimbursement.

headings.title: Annual committee evaluation and guidelines for training programs
headings.reviewNote: Charges the committee with annual evaluation and publication of standard training guidelines for licensed professions.

headings.title: Permissive agency delivery of required trafficking training
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes any board, department, or agency regulating professions subject to subsection 9 trafficking training to provide such training, with funding subject to appropriations.

headings.title: Effective and expiration dates for training committee
headings.reviewNote: Provides that subsections 5 to 10 become effective January 1, 2027, and expire on December 31, 2031.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 11 subsections for 210.1505 creating the Statewide Council Against Adult Trafficking and Commercial Sexual Exploitation of Children, membership, director, fund, training committee, professional guidelines, and effective dates.

headings.title: Retention and expungement schedules for abuse reports
headings.reviewNote: Sets retention and expungement rules: central registry and family assessments retained; malicious/retaliatory unsubstantiated reports expunged within 45 days; other unsubstantiated reports retained 10 years (mandated reporter) or 5 years; unknown-perpetrator cases retained as family assessments; unable-to-locate reports retained 18 years.

headings.title: Ninety-day written determination notice to perpetrator and parents
headings.reviewNote: Requires written notice within 90 days (120 days for sexual abuse, or completion for fatality/near-fatality) advising of probable cause/preponderance finding and 60-day review right, no finding, or unknown perpetrator.

headings.title: Reopening of investigations upon new and credible evidence
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the division to reopen a closed investigation if new, specific, and credible evidence of abuse is presented.

headings.title: Administrative review rights before Child Abuse and Neglect Review Board
headings.reviewNote: Entitles alleged perpetrators aggrieved by substantiation to request administrative review before the review board within sixty days.

headings.title: Review board proceedings and evidentiary preponderance standard
headings.reviewNote: Governs review board hearings, requiring the division to sustain its finding by a preponderance of the evidence.

headings.title: De novo judicial review in circuit court following board decision
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes individuals aggrieved by the review board decision to petition the circuit court for de novo judicial review.

headings.title: Review board notice to child or representative of review
headings.reviewNote: Requires the child abuse and neglect review board in any administrative review action to notify the child or the child's parent, guardian, or legal representative that a review has been requested.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 7 subsections for 210.152 governing retention and expungement of child abuse reports, 90/120-day written determination notices, reopening on new evidence, CANRB administrative review, preponderance standard, de novo judicial review, and notice to the child or representative.

headings.title: Creation of Child Abuse and Neglect Review Board
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Child Abuse and Neglect Review Board within social services to provide independent administrative reviews.

headings.title: Gubernatorial appointment and composition of nine-member board
headings.reviewNote: Requires appointment of nine members by the governor with senate consent, including pediatricians, psychologists, and attorneys.

headings.title: Selection of professional and citizen board members
headings.reviewNote: Permits selecting other board members from another interested profession, higher education or K-12 educators, child advocates, or parents, foster parents, or grandparents.

headings.title: Permitted participants in administrative review hearings
headings.reviewNote: Lists permitted hearing attendees including alleged perpetrators, attorneys, witnesses, and division casework staff.

headings.title: Uncompensated member service and expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Provides that board members serve without compensation but receive reimbursement for necessary travel expenses.

headings.title: Confidentiality of board records and review proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Declares all hearing records, evidence, and proceedings confidential and exempt from public inspection.

headings.title: Department rulemaking governing board review procedures
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to promulgate rules governing board operations, including member term lengths, chair selection, confidentiality, party notices, and review timelines.

headings.title: Bar on review board hearing court-adjudicated findings
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits the child abuse and neglect review board from hearing probable cause (pre-August 28, 2004) or preponderance-of-the-evidence (post-August 28, 2004) findings substantiated by court adjudication.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 8 subsections for 210.153 creating the Child Abuse and Neglect Review Board, nine gubernatorial appointments, optional member categories, hearing participants, expense reimbursement, confidentiality, mandatory rules, and exclusion of court-adjudicated findings.

headings.title: Establishment of task force on infant abuse and neglect
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Missouri Task Force on the Prevention of Infant Abuse and Neglect within the department of social services.

headings.title: Quorum requirements and voting rules for task force actions
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that official task force actions require a majority vote of a voting quorum.

headings.title: Election of task force chairperson and vice chairperson
headings.reviewNote: Requires electing a chair and vice chair from among the appointed members at the initial meeting.

headings.title: Uncompensated service and expense reimbursement subject to funds
headings.reviewNote: Provides that members serve without compensation but may be reimbursed for expenses subject to appropriations.

headings.title: Report deadline to governor and general assembly
headings.reviewNote: Directs the task force to submit its report of findings and recommendations on or before December 31, 2016.

headings.title: Required focus areas and infant abuse prevention strategies
headings.reviewNote: Directs developing recommendations to reduce infant abuse and neglect, including information sharing between the division and hospitals/birthing centers and training division and medical staff to recognize abuse signs.

headings.title: Statutory expiration of infant abuse task force
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the task force expires on January 1, 2017, or upon submission of its final report.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 7 subsections for 210.154 creating the Missouri Task Force on the Prevention of Infant Abuse and Neglect, voting rules, officers, uncompensated service, report deadlines, recommendations, and statutory expiration.

headings.title: Division public educational and child abuse prevention programs
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division to maintain continuous educational programs informing the public about child abuse and prevention resources.

headings.title: Ongoing agency staff training programs
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division to conduct ongoing training programs in relation to sections 210.110 to 210.165 for agency staff.

headings.title: Continuous statewide publicity of toll-free telephone hotline
headings.reviewNote: Requires continuous statewide publicity of the toll-free telephone number available twenty-four hours daily for reporting.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 210.155 requiring continuous public and mandated-reporter education programs, ongoing agency staff training, and continuous publicity of the 24-hour toll-free hotline.

headings.title: Division identifying data provided to state vital registrar
headings.reviewNote: Directs the division to provide identifying information regarding individuals with substantiated abuse findings to the vital registrar.

headings.title: State registrar birth record matching notifications to division
headings.reviewNote: Requires the state registrar to notify the division when birth records match identifying information of substantiated abusers.

headings.title: Confidentiality of exchanged vital statistics and registry data
headings.reviewNote: Mandates strict confidentiality for all birth records and registry data exchanged between the agencies.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority for vital records child safety matches
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the division to promulgate administrative rules to administer the data exchange with vital statistics.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 210.156 requiring data exchange between children's division and state registrar of vital statistics, confidentiality, and rulemaking.

headings.title: Mandatory appointment of guardian ad litem in abuse proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Requires court appointment of a guardian ad litem in every judicial proceeding involving allegations of child abuse or neglect.

headings.title: Discretionary guardian ad litem in section 210.152(6) reviews
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a judge, sua sponte or on party motion, to appoint a guardian ad litem for an abused or neglected child in proceedings under section 210.152(6).

headings.title: Appointment of independent legal counsel for child beginning 2028
headings.reviewNote: Establishes independent legal counsel appointments for children effective January 1, 2028, subject to legislative appropriations.

headings.title: Guardian and counsel access to relevant records and reports
headings.reviewNote: Entitles guardians ad litem and child counsel to inspect all relevant medical, school, psychological, and division reports.

headings.title: Judicial oversight, background checks, and continuity preference
headings.reviewNote: Requires judges to discharge guardians ad litem or child's counsel who fail to faithfully discharge duties, authorizes general, criminal, and FCSR background checks, and requires preference for prior appointees absent record reason.

headings.title: Award and judicial assessment of reasonable guardian fees
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes awarding reasonable attorney fees and costs to guardians ad litem, assessed against parties or county funds.

headings.title: Designation of court-appointed special advocates to assist guardian
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes court designation of trained CASA volunteer advocates to assist the guardian ad litem in investigations.

headings.title: Mandatory training program for guardians ad litem and counsel
headings.reviewNote: Requires completion of specialized child welfare and legal advocacy training prior to serving as guardian ad litem.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 8 subsections for 210.160 governing appointment of guardian ad litem and child's counsel, sua sponte appointments, 2028 appropriations condition, access to reports, duties, fees, CASA volunteer advocates, and mandatory training.

headings.title: Criminal misdemeanor penalty for general statutory violations
headings.reviewNote: Classifies general violations of child abuse reporting laws in sections 210.110 to 210.165 as class A misdemeanors.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor penalty for intentional false child abuse reports
headings.reviewNote: Classifies intentionally filing a false report of child abuse or neglect as a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Class E felony classification for repeat false reporting convictions
headings.reviewNote: Classifies second and subsequent convictions for making false child abuse reports as class E felonies.

headings.title: Hearing of prior convictions outside jury presence
headings.reviewNote: Requires evidence of prior false reporting convictions to be heard by the judge outside the hearing and presence of the jury.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 210.165 establishing criminal penalties for reporting violations, false report classifications, repeat false reporting felonies, and evidentiary hearings on prior convictions.

headings.title: Creation and seventeen-member composition of trust fund board
headings.reviewNote: Creates the 17-member Children's Trust Fund Board within the office of administration (8 senate-confirmed public members, 1 child abuse pediatrician/SAFE CARE provider, 2 representatives, 2 senators, and 4 gubernatorial appointees).

headings.title: Member terms, two-term limit, vacancies, and incumbent savings
headings.reviewNote: Sets legislative member terms, three-year public member terms (maximum two consecutive terms), vacancy filling, and protects incumbent members on August 28, 2018.

headings.title: Gubernatorial removal of public members for cause
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the governor to remove any public member for misconduct, incompetency, or neglect of duty after opportunity to be heard.

headings.title: Employment of executive director and chapter 36 staff
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the board to employ an executive director who may obtain facilities and hire chapter 36 staff within appropriations.

headings.title: Expense reimbursement from appropriated trust fund moneys
headings.reviewNote: Permits reimbursing board members for actual and necessary expenses from appropriated children's trust fund moneys.

headings.title: Compliance with public meetings sunshine law
headings.reviewNote: Requires all board business transactions to be conducted in public meetings under sections 610.010 to 610.030.

headings.title: Acceptance of federal funds, gifts, and private donations
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes accepting federal funds, gifts, and donations for deposit into the children's trust fund without committing state funds or obligating legislative continuation.

headings.title: Election of public-member chairperson and other officers
headings.reviewNote: Requires electing a chairperson from public members for a two-year term and permits electing other officers and establishing committees.
