headings.title: Mandatory disclosure in child fatality or near-fatality cases
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director of social services, upon written request, to authorize disclosing foster home information and findings in child fatality or near-fatality cases to courts, juvenile officers, law enforcement, and prosecutors.

headings.title: Disclosure of foster home records to juvenile court officers
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the division to disclose foster home information and records to juvenile officers, courts, child advocate, guardians ad litem, law enforcement, child welfare/placement agencies, prosecutors, and other government agencies with a legal need.

headings.title: Closed chapter 610 status of foster home licensing records
headings.reviewNote: Classifies foster home licensure and child care/treatment records as closed records under chapter 610, disclosable only under this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsections for 210.498 governing parental access to foster home license revocation records, disclosure procedures, director authorization, juvenile court access, and confidentiality.

headings.title: Application for foster home and child facility licensure
headings.reviewNote: Requires license applications to be submitted on division-prescribed forms detailing facility qualifications and premises.

headings.title: Mandatory contents of issued foster and facility licenses
headings.reviewNote: Requires licenses to state clearly the facility or agency name, location, permitted program type, and number, age range, and other pertinent information about children served.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 210.501 establishing child facility license application forms and required statutory license contents.

headings.title: Division rulemaking authority for foster homes and facilities
headings.reviewNote: Directs the division to promulgate and publish administrative rules governing foster homes and residential facilities under chapter 536.

headings.title: Required focus on child health, safety, and well-being
headings.reviewNote: Mandates that rules be designed to promote child health, safety, educational progress, and physical well-being.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 210.506 governing division rulemaking for child facilities, chapter 536 compliance, and promoting child well-being.

headings.title: Statutory exceptions to foster facility license requirements
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits unlicensed operation while exempting tuition-charging DESE-diploma residential schools, camps/hospitals/sanitariums, free personal guests up to 90 days, DMH-licensed mental health/DD facilities, well-known religious order/church arrangements, and state/city/county institutions.

headings.title: Prohibition on division requiring documentation from exempt entities
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits the division from demanding compliance documentation or reports from exempt schools, hospitals, or facilities.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 210.516 establishing exceptions to foster facility license requirements and barring documentation demands on exempt entities.

headings.title: Uniform departmental classification of services to children
headings.reviewNote: Requires social services, mental health, and education to establish uniform classifications of state child services.

headings.title: Mandatory interagency meetings for service coordination
headings.reviewNote: Directs state departments to hold regular interagency meetings to coordinate children's services and eliminate duplication.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 210.518 requiring uniform interagency classification of child services and interagency coordination meetings.

headings.title: Division designation of licensed child-placing agencies to inspect
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the division to designate licensed child-placing agencies to inspect and recommend foster homes for licensing.

headings.title: Division designation of political subdivisions to inspect facilities
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes designating municipal or county agencies to inspect foster homes and residential care facilities on behalf of the state.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 210.521 authorizing the division to designate private child-placing agencies or political subdivisions to inspect foster homes.

headings.title: Right to chapter 536 judicial review of final decisions
headings.reviewNote: Entitles any person aggrieved by a final division decision under sections 210.481 to 210.536 to judicial review under chapter 536.

headings.title: Establishment of formal division grievance procedures
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division to establish formal, accessible grievance procedures for licensed foster parents and applicants.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 210.526 establishing grievance procedures for foster care licensing decisions and authorizing judicial reviews.

headings.title: State payment of foster care costs and parental support liability
headings.reviewNote: Directs the division to pay foster care maintenance while holding parents liable for support according to financial ability.

headings.title: Court enforcement orders against parental assets for support costs
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes courts to enter judgment and execute against parental assets to recover delinquent foster care maintenance costs.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 210.536 governing foster care payment by the children's division, parental payment liability, and court orders against parental assets.

headings.title: Specialized foster parent authorization to purchase state insurance
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes licensed specialized foster parents caring for medically fragile children to purchase state employee health insurance.

headings.title: Mandatory documentation of specialized foster parent eligibility
headings.reviewNote: Requires submitting proof of specialized foster licensure and active child placement to qualify for insurance coverage.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 210.539 authorizing specialized foster parents to purchase state health insurance and requiring eligibility documentation.

headings.title: Mandatory pre-licensure standards and training for foster parents
headings.reviewNote: Requires the children's division to provide standards and training that prospective foster care parents shall meet before becoming licensed.

headings.title: Performance-based evaluation criteria for foster homes
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division to establish performance-based criteria to evaluate foster parent care and placement stability.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 210.542 requiring division standards and training for foster parents and performance-based evaluation criteria.

headings.title: Establishment of accessible respite care facilities for foster families
headings.reviewNote: Directs the division to establish accessible respite care services to provide temporary relief to foster parents.

headings.title: Eligible respite care facilities and licensed provider settings
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes licensed day care centers, residential treatment facilities, and licensed foster homes to provide respite care.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority for respite care standards and procedures
headings.reviewNote: Directs the division to promulgate rules and regulations governing respite care admissions, funding, and provider qualifications.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 210.545 directing the division to establish respite care facilities for foster families, eligible settings, and rulemaking.

headings.title: Definitions for child benefit funds and representative payees
headings.reviewNote: Defines child, division, money, unmet needs, vested right, and youth for child benefit accounts.

headings.title: Liability to the state for expended foster care maintenance
headings.reviewNote: Makes fiduciaries holding funds for a child liable to reimburse the state for foster care and medical costs expended.

headings.title: Division appointment as representative payee or fiduciary
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the division to accept appointment as representative payee for Social Security, veteran, or pension benefits.

headings.title: Accounting and ledger maintenance of individual child funds
headings.reviewNote: Requires accounting in the child's name, bars expending child funds for foster care maintenance or division-obligated care (permitting RRB/SSA/VA use only for unmet needs), and mandates chapter 536 accounting and theft-protection rules.

headings.title: Deposit in financial institutions and crediting of interest earnings
headings.reviewNote: Directs depositing child funds in insured financial institutions and crediting all earned interest to the child's account.

headings.title: Acceptance and management of private gifts and parental deposits
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the division to receive and hold private gifts or parental contributions for a child's special needs.

headings.title: Annual financial accounting statement to child and counsel
headings.reviewNote: Requires furnishing an annual transaction statement listing all receipts and disbursements to each child, the guardian ad litem, and the child's counsel.

headings.title: Diligence to dispose and deliver fund balances upon majority
headings.reviewNote: Directs the division to deliver accumulated account balances to the youth upon reaching eighteen or achieving emancipation.

headings.title: Five-year claims period following state treasury escheat
headings.reviewNote: Allows former foster youth or legal heirs to claim escheated funds within five years after payment into the state treasury.

headings.title: Escheat of unclaimed child funds to general revenue after five years
headings.reviewNote: Directs that unclaimed child benefit balances permanently escheat to the general revenue fund after five years.

headings.title: Non-application to general state revenues and appropriations
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that section does not apply to regular public revenues or general state appropriations.

headings.title: Contracting for federal benefit applications and rulemaking
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes social services, subject to appropriation, to contract with private individuals, law firms, nonprofits, or partnerships to apply for RRB/SSA/VA benefits and establish subsection 5 accounts, plus chapter 536 rulemaking nonseverability after August 28, 2025.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 12 subsections for 210.560 governing money held for children in state custody, joint liability, representative payee screening, unmet-needs accounting, financial institution deposits and ABLE/special needs trusts, private gifts, annual statements, disposal and escheat, five-year claims, non-application to state support revenues, and contracting for benefit applications.

headings.title: Short title of Foster Care Bill of Rights
headings.reviewNote: Designates section 210.564 as the Foster Care Bill of Rights.

headings.title: Mandatory division distribution of bill of rights to foster youth
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division to provide every school-aged foster child and foster parent with a written copy of the bill of rights.

headings.title: Enumeration of protected rights for children in foster care
headings.reviewNote: Details youth rights including safety, food, clothing, sibling visitation, medical care, education, and court participation.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 210.564 enacting the Foster Care Bill of Rights, division distribution duties, and enumerating statutory youth rights.

headings.title: Mandatory first consideration of grandparents and relatives
headings.reviewNote: Requires courts and the division to give first consideration to grandparents and relatives when placing a child in foster care.

headings.title: Definitions of adult sibling, relative, and sibling
headings.reviewNote: Defines adult sibling, relative (including nonrelatives with a close relationship such as foster or kinship caregivers of nine or more months), and sibling.

headings.title: Statutory order of preference for child relative placements
headings.reviewNote: Establishes statutory placement preference order: (1) grandparents, (2) adult siblings or parents of siblings, (3) relatives, and (4) any currently licensed foster parent capable of accepting placement.

headings.title: Specific judicial findings required to deny relative placement
headings.reviewNote: Requires the court to make specific written findings on the record if grandparent or relative placement is denied.

headings.title: Preservation of sibling bonds and joint placement preference
headings.reviewNote: Mandates making every reasonable effort to place siblings together in the same foster home unless contrary to safety.

headings.title: Prohibition on relative age as sole disqualifying placement factor
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits using the chronological age of a grandparent or relative as the sole factor in denying child placement.

headings.title: Mandatory compliance with Indian Child Welfare Act for Native children
headings.reviewNote: Directs strict compliance with federal Indian Child Welfare Act placement preferences for Native American children.

headings.title: Case-by-case non-safety foster home licensing waivers for relatives
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes granting case-by-case waivers of non-safety licensing standards to facilitate relative foster care placement.

headings.title: Duty of guardian ad litem or counsel to ascertain child wishes
headings.reviewNote: Requires the guardian ad litem or child counsel to interview the child and ascertain the child's placement preferences.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 9 subsections for 210.565 prioritizing relative and grandparent foster placements, definitions, order of preference, court findings, sibling placement, age non-discrimination, ICWA compliance, licensing waivers, and child wishes.

headings.title: Recognition of foster parents as essential care team colleagues
headings.reviewNote: Recognizes foster parents as essential colleagues on the child welfare team entitled to dignity, respect, and trust.

headings.title: Mandatory disclosure of relevant child medical and history records
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division to provide foster parents with relevant child history, behavioral issues, and medical assessments.

headings.title: Foster parent authority for daily living and extracurricular decisions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes foster parents to make routine daily living and extracurricular activity decisions under the reasonable prudent parent standard.

headings.title: Post-care updates, removal notice, reentry, and adoption rights
headings.reviewNote: Provides post-care progress info on request, two weeks' advance removal notice both ways (except emergencies), first consideration upon reentry if not relative placement, preferential section 453.070 adoption consideration, and a 60-day adoption election window.

headings.title: Mandatory advance court notice and right to be heard in proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Requires courts to provide at least two weeks advance notice of all hearings and guarantees foster parents the right to be heard.

headings.title: Access to fair and impartial grievance and appeal procedures
headings.reviewNote: Guarantees foster parents access to an impartial grievance process to appeal adverse division placement or licensing actions.

headings.title: Division provision of comprehensive ongoing foster parent training
headings.reviewNote: Directs the division to provide accessible training covering trauma-informed care, behavioral support, and cultural competence.

headings.title: Statutory definition of foster parent and resource families
headings.reviewNote: Defines foster parent as a licensed resource family providing 24-hour care for children in division custody.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 8 subsections for 210.566 enacting the Foster Parents' Bill of Rights, colleague treatment, training and full record disclosure, daily living and cultural care, removal notice and adoption preference, court hearing notice, impartial grievance access, policy training, and foster parent definition.

headings.title: County authority to establish juvenile regimented discipline program
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes first class counties with over 200,000 residents to establish boot-camp style juvenile discipline programs.

headings.title: Voter approval requirement and statutory ballot form
headings.reviewNote: Requires majority voter approval before establishing a regimented discipline program and sets forth the statutory YES/NO ballot question form.

headings.title: Effect of election and one-year resubmission bar
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the county commission to establish the program upon majority approval and bars establishment or resubmission to voters for at least one year if rejected.

headings.title: Program modeled on corrections regimented discipline program
headings.reviewNote: Permits modeling the county program after the department of corrections regimented discipline program under section 217.378.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 210.568 authorizing juvenile offender regimented discipline programs in qualifying first-class counties, voter approval and ballot form, election effect and one-year resubmission bar, and modeling on section 217.378.

headings.title: Creation of Missouri State Foster Care and Adoption Board
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Missouri State Foster Care and Adoption Board within the department of social services.

headings.title: Board membership representing foster and adoption associations
headings.reviewNote: Details voting board membership representing regional foster and adoption associations across the state.

headings.title: Two-year member terms and vacancy appointment rules
headings.reviewNote: Establishes terms of at least two years and governs appointments to fill unexpired member vacancies.

headings.title: Actual and necessary expense reimbursement for members
headings.reviewNote: Provides that board members may be reimbursed for actual and necessary travel expenses incurred.

headings.title: Public meetings compliance with chapter 610 sunshine law
headings.reviewNote: Requires all board meetings and business transactions to comply with chapter 610 public meeting laws.

headings.title: Election of chairperson, co-chairperson, and officers
headings.reviewNote: Directs the board to elect a chairperson, co-chairperson, and necessary officers from its membership.

headings.title: Board duties to review policies and recommend guidelines
headings.reviewNote: Requires procedures to review proposed division policies within 30 days, provide draft policy suggestions, and determine section 210.566 in-service training content.

headings.title: Annual written report to governor and general assembly
headings.reviewNote: Requires submitting an annual written evaluation report to the department director, governor, and legislature.

headings.title: Independent exercise of statutory powers and duties
headings.reviewNote: Directs that the board shall exercise its statutory powers and duties independently of the children's division.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 9 subsections for 210.617 creating the Missouri State Foster Care and Adoption Board, members, terms, expenses, public meetings, officers, duties, reports, and independent powers.

headings.title: Definition of appropriate public authorities under ICPC
headings.reviewNote: Defines appropriate public authorities under Article III of the Interstate Compact on the Placement of Children as the Division of Family Services (source note flags dual versions due to section 210.650 contingent effective date).

headings.title: Definition of appropriate authority in the receiving state
headings.reviewNote: Defines appropriate authority in the receiving state under Article V(a) of the compact as the Division of Family Services.

headings.title: Governor authority to appoint state compact administrator
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the governor to appoint an administrator to coordinate compact operations with other party states.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 210.630 defining Interstate Compact on the Placement of Children terms and authorizing appointment of compact administrator.

headings.title: Judicial deference to reasonable caregiver parenting decisions
headings.reviewNote: Directs courts and parties to defer to caregiver decisions made under the reasonable and prudent parent standard.

headings.title: Application of reasonable and prudent parent standard
headings.reviewNote: Requires caregivers to use the prudent parent standard when approving extracurricular and social activities for foster youth.

headings.title: Designation of onsite caregiver at residential child facilities
headings.reviewNote: Requires residential child-care facilities to designate at least one onsite staff member authorized to apply the standard.

headings.title: Relevant factors considered in caregiver activity approval
headings.reviewNote: Directs caregivers to assess child age, maturity, developmental stage, and risk level when approving activities.

headings.title: Mandatory caregiver training on reasonable prudent parenting
headings.reviewNote: Requires foster parents and residential facility staff to receive training on applying the prudent parent standard.

headings.title: Civil liability immunity for approved prudent parent activities
headings.reviewNote: Immunizes caregivers from liability for harm to a child during a caregiver-chosen activity provided the caregiver acted in accordance with the reasonable and prudent parent standard.

headings.title: Prohibition on court-ordered division funding for activities
headings.reviewNote: Bars courts from ordering the division to provide funding for extracurricular activities approved by caregivers.

headings.title: Standard for court to overturn caregiver activity decisions
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a court may overturn a caregiver's decision only after notice and hearing upon finding by clear and convincing evidence that the reasonable and prudent parent standard was violated.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 8 subsections for 210.665 establishing the reasonable and prudent parent standard for foster caregivers, judicial deference, onsite caregivers, training, liability immunity, funding limits, and overturning criteria.

headings.title: Mandatory consultation with foster children aged fourteen and older
headings.reviewNote: Requires consulting with youth aged fourteen and older in developing and updating case plans and transition plans.

headings.title: Youth selection of family support team participants
headings.reviewNote: Permits youth 14 and older to choose family support team participants (subject to division good-cause rejection) and designate one advisor and advocate for the reasonable and prudent parent standard.

headings.title: Written statement of foster youth rights and acknowledgment
headings.reviewNote: Requires providing the child a written document detailing rights to education, health, visitation, court participation, vital documents, and safety, plus a signed acknowledgment of receipt and explanation.

headings.title: Mandatory provision of vital documents upon exiting foster care
headings.reviewNote: Directs providing youth exiting care at majority with birth certificates, Social Security cards, IDs, and health records.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 210.670 requiring consultation with foster children aged fourteen and older, team participation, written rights documents, and vital documents upon aging out.

headings.title: Prohibition on APPLA permanency plans for youth under sixteen
headings.reviewNote: Bars establishing another planned permanent living arrangement (APPLA) as a permanency plan for children under sixteen.

headings.title: Specific judicial findings required to approve APPLA plans
headings.reviewNote: Requires annual judicial findings explaining why APPLA is the best permanency plan and why family placement is unachievable.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 210.675 prohibiting APPLA permanency plans for foster children under sixteen and requiring judicial findings for older youth.

headings.title: Six-month written status report and judicial dispositional review
headings.reviewNote: Requires authorized agencies holding custody to submit written status reports within six months for judicial review.

headings.title: One-thousand-foot residency bar for child who abused another
headings.reviewNote: Bars the court from returning a child determined to have abused another child to any residence within 1,000 feet of the abused child's residence, child care facility, or school until the abused child reaches age 18 (excluding siblings).

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 210.710 requiring six-month agency petitions and written status reports for court dispositional review and imposing a 1,000-foot proximity bar for a child who abused another child.

headings.title: Mandatory twelve-month permanency hearings and periodic reviews
headings.reviewNote: Requires holding a permanency hearing within twelve months of foster custody and at least annually thereafter.

headings.title: Relevant factors considered by court in permanency reviews
headings.reviewNote: Details factors considered, including parent progress, child safety, placement stability, and timeframes to reunification.

headings.title: Mandatory written findings of fact and conclusions of law
headings.reviewNote: Directs judges to issue specific written findings of fact and legal conclusions supporting all permanency determinations.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 210.720 requiring twelve-month permanency hearings for foster children in state custody, relevant factors, and written findings of fact.

headings.title: Division duties for foster placement, notice, and reunification
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division to arrange preplacement visits (except emergencies), provide full medical history, give five days' advance removal notice with written reasons, notify parents of placement, and work toward return or adoption.

headings.title: Restrictions on removing children from school premises
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits removing foster children from school buildings during class hours absent emergency protective custody orders.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 210.760 specifying six division foster placement and removal-notice duties and prohibiting removing a child from school before the end of the official school day without a court order (except under section 210.125).

headings.title: Family support team meeting timing after custody or move
headings.reviewNote: Requires a family support team meeting before or within 24 hours after the section 211.032 protective custody hearing, prior to placement actions, or within 72 hours of an emergency placement change, excluding written section 453.010(6) TPR consents.

headings.title: Permitted attendees at family support team meetings
headings.reviewNote: Lists permitted attendees including parents, counsel, foster parents, guardians ad litem, and caseworker staff.

headings.title: Execution of signed core commitments form at meeting close
headings.reviewNote: Requires completing and signing the core commitments form documenting placement and visitation plans at meeting end.

headings.title: Caseworker duty to file signed form in official case records
headings.reviewNote: Directs the assigned caseworker to file copies of the signed commitments form in the permanent child welfare record.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 210.762 mandating family support team meetings upon taking child custody, permitted attendees, commitment forms, and case records.

headings.title: Mandatory immediate reporting of missing foster children to police
headings.reviewNote: Requires reporting a missing foster child to local law enforcement and national missing child centers within two hours.

headings.title: Division protocols and staff training for runaway investigations
headings.reviewNote: Directs maintaining protocols and staff training for locating missing foster children and assessing abduction risks.

headings.title: Current photographic records of children in state custody
headings.reviewNote: Requires maintaining up-to-date photographs and descriptive information for all children in division custody.

headings.title: Law enforcement and court notifications upon locating child
headings.reviewNote: Requires notifying law enforcement, juvenile courts, and case parties immediately when a missing child is recovered.

headings.title: Twenty-four-hour reporting for missing homeless or runaway youth
headings.reviewNote: Requires children's division, child welfare, state agency, or school employees and contractors to report missing emancipated minors, homeless youth, or unaccompanied minors to law enforcement and NCMEC within 24 hours.

headings.title: Mandatory debriefing within 24 hours of recovering missing child
headings.reviewNote: Requires screening and debriefing recovered youth within twenty-four hours to identify human trafficking or abuse.

headings.title: Annual independent legislative audit of missing child compliance
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes annual independent audits to monitor department compliance with missing foster child protocols.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 7 subsections for 210.795 mandating two-hour reporting of missing foster children, ongoing search protocols, current photos, recovery notifications and in-person contact, 24-hour reporting for missing homeless/unaccompanied youth, 24-hour trafficking debriefing, and permissive annual legislative audits.

headings.title: Statutory legal presumptions of natural father paternity
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates statutory grounds establishing paternity presumptions, including marriage, attempted marriage, and acknowledgments.

headings.title: Rebuttal of paternity presumption by clear and convincing evidence
headings.reviewNote: Provides that paternity presumptions may be rebutted only by clear and convincing evidence or genetic test results.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 210.822 establishing rebuttable legal presumptions of paternity and standard of proof for rebuttal.

headings.title: Legal finding of paternity upon signed acknowledgment form
headings.reviewNote: Treats a signed section 193.215 paternity acknowledgment as a legal finding of paternity subject to written rescission within 60 days or before a support proceeding, after which court challenges are limited to fraud, duress, or material mistake of fact.

headings.title: Continuation of support obligations during revocation action
headings.reviewNote: Provides that, except for good cause shown, legal responsibilities including child support obligations shall not be suspended while an action to revoke a signed acknowledgment is pending.

headings.title: Mandatory filing of paternity acknowledgments with state bureau
headings.reviewNote: Requires filing completed paternity acknowledgments with the bureau of vital records to update birth records.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 210.823 making signed paternity acknowledgments legal findings subject to 60-day rescission and fraud/duress/mistake challenges, continuing support duties during revocation actions, and requiring bureau filing and interstate recognition.

headings.title: Husband consent and legal treatment as natural father
headings.reviewNote: Treats husband consenting in writing to physician artificial insemination as the natural father of the conceived child.

headings.title: Donor treated as not the natural father of conceived child
headings.reviewNote: Provides that semen donors providing semen to licensed physicians for artificial insemination are not legal natural fathers.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 210.824 governing husband consent for artificial insemination, treating husband as natural father, and donor rights.

headings.title: Standing to determine existence of father and child relationship
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes child, mother, presumed father, or social services to bring actions to determine legal paternity.

headings.title: Standing to establish paternity when no presumed father exists
headings.reviewNote: Lists parties authorized to bring an action to determine existence of the father-and-child relationship for a child who has no presumed father under section 210.822.

headings.title: Non-binding nature of unapproved private paternity contracts
headings.reviewNote: Provides that private paternity agreements not approved by the court do not bar subsequent paternity suits.

headings.title: Paternity actions commenced prior to birth of child
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes filing paternity actions before birth, while staying final trial until after the child's delivery.

headings.title: Mandatory boldface notice form attached to service of process
headings.reviewNote: Requires attaching a boldface Important Notice form to served paternity petitions warning of default judgment, child support, right to contest paternity, and right to request genetic testing.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsections for 210.826 governing standing for presumed and non-presumed paternity actions, non-bar of unapproved private agreements, stay of pre-birth actions, and mandatory boldface notice attached to service of process.

headings.title: Statute of limitations for bringing paternity actions
headings.reviewNote: Bars paternity actions for a child with no presumed father later than 18 years after birth, except the child may bring an action within three years after turning 18.

headings.title: Five-year retroactive child support reimbursement limit
headings.reviewNote: Limits parent's retroactive liability for past necessary support to five years preceding filing of the petition.

headings.title: Preservation of probate code inheritance limitation periods
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that paternity limitation periods do not extend probate deadlines for asserting inheritance rights.

headings.title: Mandatory boldface notice form attached to service of process
headings.reviewNote: Requires attaching a boldface Important Notice form to served petitions warning of default judgment, support obligations, right to contest paternity, and right to request genetic testing.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 210.828 setting statutes of limitations for non-presumed paternity actions, a five-year retroactive support limit, preservation of probate inheritance deadlines, and mandatory boldface service-of-process notices.

headings.title: Circuit court jurisdiction over Uniform Parentage Act actions
headings.reviewNote: Vests the circuit court with subject matter jurisdiction over all parentage actions brought under sections 210.817 to 210.852.

headings.title: Long-arm personal jurisdiction based on sexual intercourse in state
headings.reviewNote: Submits any person engaging in sexual intercourse in Missouri to state court jurisdiction for resulting paternity actions.

headings.title: Personal jurisdiction grounds for non-resident putative fathers
headings.reviewNote: Permits asserting personal jurisdiction over any person on any basis consistent with the Missouri or United States Constitution.

headings.title: Venue in county of child residence or putative father presence
headings.reviewNote: Places venue in the county where the child, mother, or alleged father resides or may be found.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 210.829 establishing circuit court jurisdiction, long-arm jurisdiction for sexual intercourse, non-resident personal jurisdiction, and venue.

headings.title: Informal pretrial paternity hearing before court master
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes informal pretrial hearings before a commissioner or master to evaluate evidence and recommend settlement.

headings.title: Court authority to compel party and witness testimony under oath
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the court to compel testimony and contempt sanctions against witnesses refusing to testify.

headings.title: Abrogation of physician-patient privilege for pregnancy medical facts
headings.reviewNote: Abrogates physician privilege regarding medical facts concerning pregnancy and the probable period of conception.

headings.title: Court authority to require presumed father support bond
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the court on party motion to require a presumed father to post bond guaranteeing payment of support between action commencement and final disposition, considering section 210.841(5) factors.

headings.title: Issuance of temporary child support orders pending final trial
headings.reviewNote: Requires entering a temporary child support order upon party motion when clear and convincing evidence establishes a section 210.822 presumption or section 210.823 acknowledgment, retroactive to motion service or presumption/acknowledgment.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsections for 210.832 governing informal pretrial hearings before masters, compelled testimony with use immunity, non-privileged physician pregnancy testimony, presumed father support bonds, and temporary support orders.

headings.title: Mandatory court-ordered genetic and blood testing upon request
headings.reviewNote: Requires the court upon party request to order mother, child, and alleged father to submit to genetic testing.

headings.title: Party requests for independent genetic testing verification
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the court, upon reasonable request by a party, to order independent blood tests performed by other qualified experts.

headings.title: Evidentiary sanctions and resolving issues upon test refusal
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes contempt findings or resolving paternity against a party refusing to submit to court-ordered genetic tests.

headings.title: Dismissal of paternity action upon conclusive genetic exclusion
headings.reviewNote: Directs dismissal of paternity proceedings if genetic test results conclusively exclude the alleged father.

headings.title: Certified chain of custody documentation as admissible evidence
headings.reviewNote: Makes certified chain of custody documents competent evidence establishing specimen authenticity without live testimony.

headings.title: Admissibility of pretrial administrative genetic test results
headings.reviewNote: Applies chain of custody and evidentiary standards to tests conducted prior to judicial action.

headings.title: Statutory qualifications and definition of genetic testing experts
headings.reviewNote: Defines expert qualified to perform and interpret parentage genetic tests under accredited standards.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 7 subsections for 210.834 governing court-ordered genetic blood tests, independent tests, refusal sanctions, exclusion orders, chain of custody documentation, and defining testing experts.

headings.title: Master pretrial recommendation of paternity and support terms
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the hearing master to recommend settlement terms, dismissal, or voluntary paternity agreements.

headings.title: Entry of court judgment upon party acceptance of recommendation
headings.reviewNote: Directs entering final judgment in accordance with master recommendations if all parties accept the proposed terms.

headings.title: Trial setting and genetic testing upon party refusal of recommendation
headings.reviewNote: Directs setting the matter for trial and ordering genetic testing if any party rejects the master's recommendation.

headings.title: Guardian ad litem authority to accept or reject recommendations
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the child's guardian ad litem to accept or reject master recommendations in the child's best interests.

headings.title: Termination of informal proceedings upon impasse
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes terminating pretrial proceedings and scheduling formal trial when settlement cannot be reached.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsections for 210.838 governing pretrial recommendations by masters, party acceptance, refusal effects, guardian ad litem powers, and trial settings.

headings.title: Parentage civil trial procedure and supreme court rules
headings.reviewNote: Provides that parentage actions are civil proceedings governed by the Missouri rules of civil procedure.

headings.title: Inadmissibility of sexual access outside probable conception period
headings.reviewNote: Bars evidence of mother's sexual access with other men outside the medically probable conception period.

headings.title: Conditions for evidence of other men's sexual access
headings.reviewNote: Conditions evidence of another man's sexual intercourse with the mother on blood testing if outside jurisdiction, mandatory impleader 60 days before trial if subject to jurisdiction, or 30-day notice if outside.

headings.title: Non-jury bench trials and genetic presumption standards
headings.reviewNote: Eliminates any right to a jury trial and sets preponderance of the evidence as the burden of proof on all issues unless a section 210.822 presumption applies.

headings.title: Entry of default judgment upon failure to appear or answer
headings.reviewNote: Requires the court to enter judgment by default against any party failing to file an answer or appear within the prescribed time.

headings.title: Admissibility of pregnancy, birth, and genetic testing bills
headings.reviewNote: Admits copies of paid or unpaid bills for pregnancy, childbirth, or genetic testing without third-party foundation testimony as prima facie evidence if provided to all parties at least seven days before trial.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsections for 210.839 governing parentage civil trial procedures, evidence admissibility, non-jury trials, default judgments, and medical bill evidence.

headings.title: Judgment or order determining existence of parent-child relationship
headings.reviewNote: Directs entering judgment declaring parentage and resolving custody, visitation, and child support obligations.

headings.title: Court direction to amend birth certificate to reflect father
headings.reviewNote: Directs the vital records bureau to amend the child's birth certificate to conform with the court's paternity judgment.

headings.title: Inclusion of Social Security numbers and parenting provisions
headings.reviewNote: Requires inclusion of party Social Security numbers and orders regarding legal custody and parenting schedules.

headings.title: Periodic child support payments and lump-sum exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Requires support judgments to direct periodic payments, allowing lump-sum or trust awards in the child's best interests.

headings.title: Rebuttable presumption of support amount under Rule 88.01
headings.reviewNote: Applies a rebuttable presumption that child support calculated under Supreme Court Rule 88.01 is correct.

headings.title: Relevant statutory factors in determining child support awards
headings.reviewNote: Details factors considered, including financial resources of parents, child physical needs, and educational costs.

headings.title: Retroactive child support awards to date of service
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes awarding retroactive child support back to the date the petition was served on the parent.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 7 subsections for 210.841 governing paternity judgments, birth certificate amendments, Social Security inclusion, periodic support, Rule 88.01 presumptions, support factors, and retroactive support.

headings.title: Enforcement remedies for paternity child support judgments
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes all statutory remedies, income withholding, and liens to enforce parentage child support judgments.

headings.title: Support payments directed to circuit clerk or payment center
headings.reviewNote: Directs support payments to be made through the circuit clerk or family support payment center.

headings.title: Civil contempt sanctions for willful failure to obey support orders
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes civil contempt proceedings and incarceration for willful failure to comply with paternity support decrees.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 210.843 governing enforcement of paternity support judgments, payments through circuit clerk or payment center, and civil contempt.

headings.title: Modification of support decree upon substantial changed circumstances
headings.reviewNote: Allows modifying support decrees only upon substantial and continuing changed circumstances making terms unreasonable, establishing a 20% Rule 88.01 variance as a prima facie showing.

headings.title: Application of Rule 88.01 once modification burden is met
headings.reviewNote: Requires determining child support in conformity with Supreme Court Rule 88.01 criteria once the party seeking modification meets the subsection 1 burden of proof.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 210.845 governing modification of parentage child support decrees, changed circumstances burden, and twenty percent Rule 88.01 variance.

headings.title: Grandparent liability for support when parent is an unemancipated minor
headings.reviewNote: Holds maternal and paternal grandparents liable for support of grandchildren when the father or mother is an unemancipated minor.

headings.title: Relevant factors in determining grandparent support obligations
headings.reviewNote: Details factors considered, including financial resources of grandparents, minor parents, and grandchild needs.

headings.title: Non-application of Rule 88.01 guidelines to grandparent support
headings.reviewNote: Provides that Supreme Court Rule 88.01 child support guidelines do not apply to grandparent support calculations.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 210.847 imposing child support liability on grandparents when parents are minors, determining support amounts, and excluding Rule 88.01.

headings.title: Petition to set aside paternity judgment based on genetic exclusion
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes an adjudicated father to petition to set aside a paternity and support judgment based on scientific genetic testing.

headings.title: Mandatory petitioner affidavit and genetic testing proof
headings.reviewNote: Requires attaching an affidavit asserting newly discovered genetic evidence proving non-paternity.

headings.title: Evidentiary hearing and court-ordered independent genetic testing
headings.reviewNote: Directs the court to hold an evidentiary hearing and order independent confirmatory genetic testing.

headings.title: Setting aside paternity finding and extinguishing future support
headings.reviewNote: Directs setting aside paternity and extinguishing future child support upon confirmed genetic exclusion.

headings.title: Prohibition on setting aside judgments involving adopted children
headings.reviewNote: Provides that this section shall not apply to grant relief to the parent of any adopted child.

headings.title: Finding of material mistake of fact setting aside judgment
headings.reviewNote: Deems confirmed genetic non-paternity a material mistake of fact warranting judicial relief from judgment.

headings.title: Prohibition on retroactive recovery of previously paid support
headings.reviewNote: Bars setting aside orders from creating causes of action to recover child support paid prior to petition filing.

headings.title: Expungement of criminal nonsupport records after set-aside
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a petitioner who pled guilty to or was found guilty of section 568.040 criminal nonsupport for a non-biological child to obtain court expungement of arrest, plea, trial, and conviction records after paternity set-aside.

headings.title: Family support division tracking and annual report to legislature
headings.reviewNote: Directs the family support division to track cases and submit annual reports to the general assembly on set-aside petitions.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 9 subsections for 210.854 governing petitions to set aside paternity and support judgments, affidavits and DNA testing, hearings, relief and arrearage extinguishment, adoption exclusion, material mistake of fact, no reimbursement recovery, expungement of criminal nonsupport records, and annual division tracking.

headings.title: County property tax levy for children's services upon voter approval
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes counties to submit a property tax levy up to twenty-five cents per hundred dollars valuation to voters.

headings.title: Deposit of tax revenues in special community children's services fund
headings.reviewNote: Requires depositing all tax proceeds into a dedicated county fund used exclusively for youth mental health and support services.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 210.860 authorizing county property tax levies for community children's services upon voter approval and creating dedicated county funds.

headings.title: Establishment and appointment of nine-member board of directors
headings.reviewNote: Directs county governing bodies to appoint a nine-member board of directors to administer the children's services fund.

headings.title: Board officers, treasurer bond, and local spending control
headings.reviewNote: Requires electing a chairman, vice chairman, treasurer (with surety bond or comparable insurance), and other officers, and bars state legislative spending mandates without local majority vote (excluding charter counties over 950,000).

headings.title: Board contracting authority with public and nonprofit agencies
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes contracting with licensed public or nonprofit agencies to deliver child mental health and counseling services.

headings.title: Authorized expenditure purposes for children's mental health care
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates permitted expenditures including crisis intervention, counseling, outpatient treatment, and abuse prevention.

headings.title: Voter approval required to add new statutory services
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits counties (excluding charter counties over 950,000) and St. Louis City from adding post-levy statutory services beyond subsection 4 without voter approval in the same manner as the original levy.

headings.title: Statutory prohibitions and restrictions on fund expenditures
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits expending community children's services fund revenues for inpatient medical, psychiatric, or chemical dependency services, or for transportation services.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsections for 210.861 establishing the nine-member Community Children's Services Board, officers and treasurer bond, agency contracting and conflict rules, authorized youth services, voter approval for adding services, and prohibitions on inpatient and transportation spending.

headings.title: Creation of Juvenile Information Governance Commission
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Juvenile Information Governance Commission.

headings.title: Composition and appointment of commission members
headings.reviewNote: Specifies 13 commission members: nine state agency, judicial, highway patrol, and IT officials, plus two juvenile judges and two juvenile officers appointed by the supreme court chief justice.

headings.title: Commission duties for interagency information sharing
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commission to authorize categories of information shared under section 210.865, provide vision, strategy, policy approval, and oversight, and permits appointing technical and policy subcommittees.

headings.title: State courts administrator as commission chairperson
headings.reviewNote: Designates the state courts administrator or a designee to chair the commission.

headings.title: Semiannual meeting minimum and majority quorum
headings.reviewNote: Requires the commission to meet at the chair's determination at least semiannually and establishes a majority of members as a quorum.

headings.title: Uncompensated service of commission members
headings.reviewNote: Provides that no member of the commission shall receive compensation for performing commission duties.

headings.title: Preparation, distribution, and filing of official minutes
headings.reviewNote: Requires the chair to prepare official minutes of all meetings, distribute them to members, and file them with the state courts administrator.

headings.title: Annual January first report to general assembly
headings.reviewNote: Requires transmitting an annual report summarizing commission findings to the general assembly on January 1, 2002, and each January 1 thereafter.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 8 subsections for 210.870 creating the 13-member Juvenile Information Governance Commission, authorizing information-sharing categories and oversight, designating the state courts administrator as chair, setting semiannual meetings and quorum, uncompensated service, official minutes, and annual legislative reports.

headings.title: Evaluation of laws affecting incarcerated parents and children
headings.reviewNote: Directs the Missouri children's services commission to evaluate state laws and policies affecting incarcerated parents and their children, emphasizing child custody and visitation.

headings.title: Informing policymakers on children of incarcerated parents
headings.reviewNote: Requires informing legislators and policymakers about problems facing children of incarcerated parents and the value of coordinating penal policies and child welfare goals.

headings.title: Legislative proposals and community care for incarcerated parents
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes recommending legislative proposals and state or local programs for children of incarcerated parents, including alternative sentencing laws and community-based care facilities to maintain parental custody.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 210.875 directing the Missouri Children's Services Commission to evaluate laws affecting incarcerated parents and their children, inform policymakers, and recommend legislative proposals and community-based care programs.

headings.title: Short title of Family Care Safety Act
headings.reviewNote: Designates sections 210.900 to 210.936 as the Family Care Safety Act.

headings.title: Definitions for family care safety registry
headings.reviewNote: Defines 13 terms including child-care, elder-care, mental health, and personal-care providers and workers, department, employer, patrol, and related child/elder care (source note flags section 289.005 repealed in 1995).

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 210.900 enacting the Family Care Safety Act and defining statutory registry terms.

headings.title: Establishment of Family Care Safety Registry and toll-free line
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Family Care Safety Registry and toll-free telephone access line to protect children, elderly, and vulnerable adults.

headings.title: Registry contents including criminal records, abuse lists, and licenses
headings.reviewNote: Details registry contents combining criminal history records, sex offender registries, child abuse findings, and employee disqualification lists.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 210.903 establishing the Family Care Safety Registry, toll-free access line, and registry background check contents.

headings.title: Mandatory registration form and required contents
headings.reviewNote: Requires child-care, elder-care, personal-care, and mental health workers hired on or after specified dates to complete a department registration form containing valid SSN, appeal-right info, and signed background-check and employment-release consents.

headings.title: Fifteen-day filing deadline and class B misdemeanor penalty
headings.reviewNote: Requires workers to complete registration within 15 days of beginning employment and makes failing to submit without good cause a class B misdemeanor.

headings.title: Registration fees and employer payment authorization
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes fees for background check processing, payable by the applicant or reimbursable by the employer.

headings.title: Automatic registration for licensed foster and adoptive parents
headings.reviewNote: Provides that persons licensed as foster parents or certified for adoption are automatically registered in the registry.

headings.title: Voluntary registration for informal caregivers and volunteers
headings.reviewNote: Permits individuals not mandated to register, including private caregivers and volunteers, to register voluntarily.

headings.title: Exemption for family members providing care to relatives
headings.reviewNote: Exempts individuals providing care exclusively to children or elders related by blood or marriage from mandatory registration.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsections for 210.906 requiring caregiver registration forms and contents, setting a 15-day deadline with class B misdemeanor penalty, governing check fees, automatic foster-licensee registration, voluntary registration, and related-care exemptions.

headings.title: Department verification and interagency database background checks
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department upon receiving registration forms to cross-reference highway patrol records, sex offender registries, and abuse registries.

headings.title: Inclusion of verified background check findings in registry
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to enter verified criminal history and administrative disqualification findings into the registry profile.

headings.title: Written notification of registry determination to registrant
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to notify each registrant in writing of the results of the determination recorded on the registry.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 210.909 governing department verification duties, background database checks, and written notification of registry results.

headings.title: Authorized release of background information to inquiring callers
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes releasing registry background information to employers, parents, and caregivers upon telephone or online request.

headings.title: Mandatory disclosure to requesters regarding background scope
headings.reviewNote: Requires informing requesters of the background databases searched and limitation to state records.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalty for unlawful commercial or personal misuse
headings.reviewNote: Classifies using registry information for unauthorized commercial or personal harassment purposes as a class B misdemeanor.

headings.title: Written confirmation notice to registrant upon background disclosure
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to send written notice to the registrant whenever their background information is disclosed to an employer.

headings.title: Staff immunity and prohibition on selling the registry
headings.reviewNote: Grants DHSS staff civil and criminal immunity for providing registry information absent bad faith or ill intent, and prohibits the department from selling the registry or any portion of it.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsections for 210.921 governing release of registry information, caller disclosures, misuse penalties, written notifications, and employee liability immunity.

headings.title: Short title of Safe Place for Newborns Act
headings.reviewNote: Designates section 210.950 as the Safe Place for Newborns Act of 2002.

headings.title: Definitions for safe place for newborns act
headings.reviewNote: Defines hospital, maternity home, newborn safety incubator, nonrelinquishing parent, pregnancy resource center, and relinquishing parent.

headings.title: Parental prosecution immunity for voluntary newborn relinquishment
headings.reviewNote: Bars prosecuting a parent under sections 568.030, 568.032, 568.045, or 568.050 for voluntarily relinquishing an unharmed child up to 90 days old to a newborn safety incubator or specified hospital, maternity home, pregnancy center, fire, EMS, or police personnel.

headings.title: Parent anonymity protection and restricted disclosure list
headings.reviewNote: Exempts relinquishing parents from providing identifying information, bars coercion or state efforts to locate them, and restricts disclosure of obtained information to eight enumerated recipients.

headings.title: Receiving provider duty to take custody and arrange hospital care
headings.reviewNote: Requires authorized personnel to take physical custody without a court order of a child reasonably believed to be no more than 90 days old and arrange immediate transport to the nearest licensed hospital if delivered elsewhere.

headings.title: Hospital medical screening, testing, and newborn treatment
headings.reviewNote: Requires hospitals to perform necessary medical treatment and promptly report infant delivery to the children's division.

headings.title: Public notice, thirty-day parentage window, and registry check
headings.reviewNote: Requires juvenile officer public notice in TPR proceedings, gives parents 30 days to identify themselves and establish paternity/maternity, and mandates checking the section 192.016 putative father registry.

headings.title: Nonrelinquishing parent thirty-day deadline and TPR
headings.reviewNote: Requires a nonrelinquishing parent to take steps to establish parentage within 30 days of notice, allows termination of parental rights upon failure, and directs hospitals to refer inquiring parents to the division and juvenile court.

headings.title: Civil and criminal liability immunity for receiving providers
headings.reviewNote: Grants receiving personnel civil, criminal, and administrative immunity for accepting physical custody in good faith, excluding negligent or intentional post-acceptance acts or omissions.

headings.title: Division public educational awareness and helpline duties
headings.reviewNote: Directs the division to maintain public educational campaigns and toll-free telephone information regarding safe relinquishment.

headings.title: Affirmative defense to child abandonment and endangerment charges
headings.reviewNote: Establishes voluntary relinquishment of a child no more than one year old under this section as an affirmative defense to prosecution under sections 568.030, 568.032, 568.045, and 568.050.

headings.title: Preservation of protective custody procedures under section 210.125
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that safe relinquishment provisions do not conflict with or supersede emergency protective custody laws.

headings.title: Establishment of Safe Place for Newborns Fund in state treasury
headings.reviewNote: Creates the dedicated Safe Place for Newborns Fund in the state treasury solely for installing newborn safety incubators, with nonreversion and interest crediting.

headings.title: State general revenue matching funds up to $10,000 per box
headings.reviewNote: Requires Missouri to provide general revenue matching moneys of up to $10,000 for each newborn safety incubator installed.

headings.title: Department of health and senior services rulemaking authority
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to promulgate rules and regulations governing newborn safety box standards and implementation.
